title: A Heuristic Statistical Testing Based Approach for Encrypted Network Traffic Identification

value.name: Authors own lab traffic (SSL/DNS/HTTP from lab gateway; SSH from public honeypot trace; Freegate/Ultrasurf/Custom Unknown from controlled environment)
value.quote: For SSL, DNS, and HTTP, we used real traffic traces collected at our labs gateway...unknown protocols...were collected in a controlled environment

datasets_evaluated.evidence: For SSL, DNS, and HTTP, we used real traffic traces collected at our labs gateway. As for unknown protocols (Freegate, Ultrasurf, and Custom Unknown), they were collected in a controlled environment

label_source.evidence: we simply used the port numbers to do the labeling work, which is used for supervised learning

label_feature_overlap.evidence: we removed four features, i.e. source/destination IP addresses and source/destination port numbers, to ensure that detection results are not dependent on such biased features

value: NIST randomness P-values from payload bytes: Monobit test, Frequency Block test, Cumulative sums test, Discrete Fourier transform test (4 features for payload < 128 bytes; 8 features otherwise)
features_used.evidence: We list four tests that are employed to extract features of encrypted bitflow...Monobit test, Frequency (Block) test, Cumulative sums test, Discrete Fourier transform test

feature_groups.evidence: N bytes of payload from each pcap file are extracted using our handshake skipping method to pass to the modified NIST test suite

model_family.evidence: ML-based classifier makes use of C4.5 algorithm to build classification trees

metrics.evidence: Precision = TP/(TP + FP) Recall = TP/(TP + FN) F1 (F-measure) = 2 x Precision x Recall...False Positive Rate (FPR)

granularity.evidence: each packet to different bidirectional flow...each pcap file only contains one biflow

first_n_packets.evidence: starting with the last packet, checking if its length is greater than the threshold until a packet larger than the threshold is found
